frequency_question: How often do central bank governors with the statutory power to set a countercyclical capital buffer above zero actually raise it above zero during a non-crisis economic expansion window?
membership_rule: Includes G20 central banks with an operational CCyB framework between 2016 and 2026; excludes emergency crisis deployments (like the 2020 pandemic drops) or purely mechanical formula-based automatic stabilizers.

cases.name: Bank of England CCyB active deployment
Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB active deployment
Swiss National Bank CCyB active deployment

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 12 major advanced economies tracked; 5 utilized discretionary upward adjustments outside of immediate crisis response.
known_gaps: Varying definitions of macroprudential stance across different legal frameworks.
skeleton: Active G20/advanced economy jurisdictions possessing the CCyB tool evaluated across their post-Basel III implementation phases.
multiplier: 5 positive actions out of approximately 12 jurisdictions that eventually activated the buffer above 0% during non-crisis expansionary intervals.
validity_reason: Macroprudential governance frameworks and institutional risk appetites evolve slowly over multi-year structural cycles.
